Q: Thanks for taking the time to speak with me today. This recorded statement is about the collision you were
involved in. Do you understand that this call is being recorded?
A: Yes, I understand.
Q: Please state your full name and the location where the accident happened.
A: I'd rather not give my full name on a recording, but I can confirm I was driving. It happened at a busy intersection
here in Houston, Texas.
Q: That's fine. Can you walk me through what you were doing right before the impact?
A: I was making a left turn across the opposite lanes. I had my signal on and I waited for a gap in traffic. Then a
vehicle came toward me from the other direction, and it hit the front passenger side of my car.
Q: Did you see that vehicle before you started your turn?
A: I saw headlights further back, but I thought there was more dsitance than there was. I should have waited longer.
Q: Were you injured?
A: Yes. I hit my head on the window frame and I've had headaches, dizziness, and trouble concentrating since then.
A doctor told me I have a concussion.
Q: Have you seen a medical provider since the accident?
A: Yes, I went to urgent care the same day and I've had follow-up visits. I'm still having symptoms, so I'm taking time
off work.
Q: Thank you. Is there anything else you'd like to add about how the collision happened?
A: Only that I'm sorry it happened and I hope the other driver is okay too. I'm willing to provide my medical records.
Q: Thank you for your cooperation. This concludes the statement.
</page>

it is the loss date. Examples: "Date of loss:", "Crash date:", "Date of injury:", "the collision on".
